Bare/en Qian collides: Gao Jun/潛 (N. Qi), Zhang Qian 張潛 (Jin), Li Qian 李蒨 (Later Zhou), Sima Qian 司馬遷, and Grand Herald 騫 (Han); different surnames and eras.
en:Zhuo covers merchant clans 卓氏 and 濁氏, Dong Zhuo 董卓, Yuan Zhuo 袁濯, and Yu Zhuo 庾倬; surnames/given names and eras all differ.
Liao bare 蘇: AD 1063 soldier ≠ AD 1070 Tiyin ≠ early-dynasty royal/statesman 蘇 (085) ≠ AD 916 royal sibling 蘇 (087); prior seps bind these pairs.
AD 1063 guard 護衛蘇 is not Tiyin Su or the early Liao royal 蘇 records; prior seps bind 112 from 062/085/087.
Both Liao 蘇 in AD 1063 military contexts (soldier vs 護衛); one-character name with no office/kin bridge beyond the year.
Both 霞抹 in Liao (officer AD 1063; Prince of Liucheng AD 1076); no dossier link proving promotion from unnamed officer to 柳城郡王.
Bare 霞抹 officer (AD 1063) vs Yelu Xiamo 耶律霞抹 official (AD 1085–1094); shared personal name only.
Prince of Liucheng 霞抹 (AD 1076) vs Yelu Xiamo official (AD 1085–1094); may be one Yelu, but 086 lacks the princely title.
Both 周昌子 in Han; date anchors BC 195–180 vs BC 149 and kinship-only labeling leave identity unproven.
Both 黃八 in Liao; 114 is a household slave under AD 1032–1055, while 067 has only a dynasty-wide span and no role bridge.
Eastern Wei 平陽公 (AD 543–549) vs Northern Qi 平陽王 (AD 549–550) may be one elevation at the Qi founding, but ranks differ (公≠王) and dossier gives no personal name.

en:Zhou spans Shang tyrant 紂 (beiqishu:003:p023 group), Duke of Zhou 周公/周 (hanshu:088:p011 group), Zhou Yu 周瑜 (AD 208 Wu), Zhou Xie 周緤 (early Han), Ma Zhou 馬周 (Tang AD 645), and Yuwen Zhou 宇文冑 (Northern Zhou AD 580)—not one person.
Shun-era minister/judge Boyi (hanshu:076:p057 / hanshu:025:p091 / liaoshi:061:p003) is not Shang recluse Bo Yi (shiji:061:p010 / hanshu:076:p113 group).
Chapter-local prior separation: Shun minister Boyi ≠ Shang aristocrat/recluse Boyi.
Prior separation binds Shang-recluse Bo Yi (beiqishu:047:p035 group) off Shun-minister Boyi.
Han general 王音 (hanshu:011:p056 group) ≠ Five Dynasties military 王殷 (jiuwudaishi:130:p013 group) ≠ Northern Han rebel 王隱 (xinwudaishi:070:p052).
Han 王音 is not Later Liang courtier 王殷 (xinwudaishi:044:p009).
Later Liang 王殷 (AD 907–912) is not Northern Han 王隱 (AD 962).
耶律室魯 (~AD 1003–1012 via 060/081/094) ≠ 耶律釋魯 military AD 916 ≠ 耶律適祿 (AD 1055–1120) ≠ 耶律釋魯 yuyue/King of Sui (AD 900–916).
General 耶律室魯 (AD 969–979) is not 釋魯 or 適祿; prior separations bind these pairs.
Both 耶律釋魯 in early Liao, but prior separation remains binding despite the shared name.
en:Li Yu spans 李璵 (Northern Wei/Qi), 李瑀 (Tang prince), 李遇 and 李鬱 (Later Liang), 李愚 (Later Tang councillor group), and 李禹 (Western Han)—six distinct men.
en:Liu Zan spans Eastern Wei 瓚, Jin 劉贊 (libationer), Five Dynasties 劉讚, Liao 劉贊 (AD 988), Shu Han prince 劉瓚, and Later Liang 刘璩—not one person.
Posthumous Zhuangque links Wang Wudang 王無黨 (壯愨), Wu Jinyi 吳進義 (壯愨), and Xiang Ke 祥珂 (莊愨)—three Qing men with different personal names and careers.
Wei cavalry Feng Jing (son of Feng Wuzhe), BC 142 Grand Administrator Feng Jing, and Shiji Han official Feng Jing (BC 180–157) remain distinct under prior separations.
Prior separations keep Wei cavalry Feng Jing, BC 142 Grand Administrator, and bare Han official 025 apart.
Sun Wu 孫 (BC ~500 strategist) is prior-separated from surname-only military writer 孫 and from Zhoushu’s AD 580 allusive 孫 exemplar; one-character 孫 is unsafe to merge.
馬郁 (Fanyang writer/diplomat AD 897–898) and 馬鬱 (Yan/Jin official AD 906) share English Ma Yu but have different Chinese given characters; dossier supplies no bridge equating 郁 with 鬱.
Beiqishu Bo Yi is a legendary name-only stub; may be the Shang recluse but has no linking deed.
Name-only Bo Yi stub could also allude to the Shun-era minister Boyi.
Hanshu:065 Boyi lacks role/date beyond 伯夷.
Hanshu:065 Boyi stub could refer to either legendary Boyi.
Hanshu:089 Boyi is a legendary stub without Shang-recluse or Shun-minister markers.
Hanshu:089 Boyi stub could refer to either legendary Boyi.
Three 伯夷 stubs lack differentiating deeds; they may coincide with each other or with either legendary Boyi, but the dossier cannot prove it.
Both 王殷; Later Liang courtier AD 907–912 may be an early stage of the Later Tang–Zhou general (130/011/050 group), but the dossier gives no shared office, native place, or continuous career link.
Both 耶律室魯; 072 is a general AD 969–979, while 060/081/094 are the ~AD 1003–1012 Prince of Han / Northern Great King career—possible long career, but 072 lacks 乙辛隱 / 韓王 anchors.
All are titled King of Hengshan / 衡山王 only; one is marked rebel and one is dated BC 124, but none supplies a personal name to confirm a single holder.
Both are Sala 撒剌 in Liao at AD 1077 (military officer card and named-individual card); no conflicting titles or kin.

en:Chong only: Wang Chong 王沖 (Chen), legendary 重, Peng Chong 彭宠, Guo Chong 郭崇, Liu Chong/Min 劉崇/劉旻, Zhang Chong 張充, He Chong 何充, Lu Chong 盧重, Yelü kin 沖, Jiang Chong 江充, Wei prince 崇, and Later Han Hedong 崇 are distinct; many pairs already prior-separated.
Temple 顯祖/Xianzu reused for Northern Qi Gao Yang/Wenxuan (AD 550–559), Northern Wei Emperor Xianwen (AD 465–476), and Later Han Zhang Sheng Emperor (AD 947).
Northern Qi Xianzu (AD 550–559) is not the undated Weishu Emperor Xianzu stub spanning AD 386–534.
Later Han Xian Zu / Zhang Sheng Emperor (AD 947) is not the Weishu Emperor Xianzu stub.
Qing posthumous 文恪/Wenke is reused for Shen Chu 沈初, Wan Chengfeng 萬承風, Quan Qing 全慶, Sun Yuwen 孫毓汶, Zailing 載齡, En Cheng 恩承, and Chongli 崇禮.
en:Li Ji spans 李籍, 利幾, 酈寄, 酈將軍/Li Ji, 李勣, 李及, 李己, 李霨, and 李几—distinct persons across Wei–Qing; prior separations bind the major pairs including 酈寄 ≠ 酈將軍.
淮南王/King of Huainan is a reused title without personal names; prior separations already bind most pairs, and shiji:059:p026 (BC 124) adds no identifying name.
Mid-century Tiebu 貼不 / Prince of Wei cluster (AD 1032–1059) is not the AD 1101–1125 Prince of Wei Tiebu who fathers a son in liaoshi:031.
AD 1063 Tiebu 貼不 (衛王) is not the late-Liao AD 1101–1125 Prince of Wei Tiebu.

Sala 撒剌 names an AD 967 deer-keeper, the AD 1077 officer (merged with liaoshi:062:p030), Yelü Xieniechi’s courtesy name (AD 916–938), and a distinct AD 918 kinsman; prior separations bind these lines.
Temple Ruizong 睿宗 reused for Ming (AD 1567), Tang Emperor Ruizong (AD 710–712), and Yuan Tolui; Ming≠Yuan already prior-separated.
Southern Qi 建安王 (AD 483–493) is not the Liu Song Prince of Jian'an (AD 420–479).
Liu Song 建安王 (AD 420–479) is not the Southern Qi Prince of Jian'an (AD 479–502).
Both labeled Emperor Xianzu 顯祖; Wei Xianwen group is AD 465–471 while weishu:098 only has the broad AD 386–534 span and no polity/posthumous match.
Both 貼不 in Liao near AD 1059–1063, but mid-century cluster uses 魏王/魏國王/吳王 while 022 is 衛王; dossier lacks a career bridge.
Both 於成龍 Qing officials with overlapping Kangxi dates (AD 1682/1688/1690), but neither card supplies native place or office detail to confirm one career versus contemporaries.
Both Southern Qi 建安王 with overlapping windows (AD 483–493 and AD 479–502), but title-only with no personal name.
Both Northern Wei 西河王/Prince of Xihe in AD 520–540 / 530–540; no personal name to confirm one holder.

English Tang covers six identities: Goguryeo King 湯 (AD 560); Shang founder 湯 (Cheng Tang group); legendary Yao/唐; Western Han Qing King Liu Tang 頃王湯 (BC 94); bare Han official 湯; and Zhang Tang 張湯. Prior separations already bind most pairs; Liu Tang remains distinct from all other clusters.

Dilu romanization spans 的魯/敵魯/的錄/滌魯/敵祿: ancestor, hawk-keeper, rebel, Yelu Hou’s cousin 的錄, Prince Zunning, mother of Haili, Yelü Dilu, physician, yilijin father of the Heavenly Emperor, and chancellor. Distinct Chinese forms, roles, and priors forbid collapse; 077:p026 (的錄) is not the 的魯/敵魯 set.

楊氏 / Lady Yang labels unrelated women: Western Jin Empress Yang (AD 299); Later Zhou consort 淑妃楊氏; Yuan mother of Han Lin'er; Northern Wei Mad Aunt; Later Liang consort Guangxiao; Northern Zhou Tianyuan Grand Empress. Shared surname label only.
伯父 is only a paternal-uncle kinship label: Tang Lingze 唐令則 (Sui), Liuge 留哥 (Liao), Shen Zhenji 沈貞吉 (Ming), Yuan Xun 袁洵 (Liu-Song), and unnamed uncle of Men Wen'ai (Northern Wei) are distinct persons.
Yuting romanization only: Sun Yuting’s given 玉庭 vs Sushun’s courtesy 雨亭 vs Ding Ruchang’s courtesy 禹廷; distinct Qing identities (prior already separates Sushun from Ding).

English Dou Yi covers three Chinese names: Later Zhou 竇儼 (145), Later Zhou 竇儀 (148/xinwudaishi:031 group), and Northern Zhou 竇毅 (zhoushu 008/009 group). Priors already separate 儼↔儀 and 儀↔毅; 儼≠毅 as well.
English Ting only: Zu Ting 祖珽 (Northern Qi), Si Kongting 司空頲 (late Tang–Liang), Jin Ting 亭 (Western Han), Su Ting 蘇頲 (Tang). Shared romanized given name; distinct surnames and eras.
Wang Zhi romanization spans 王質 (Tang-era father, AD 885–888), 王植 (Qing official, AD 1842–1843), and 王直 (Ming statesman, AD 1450).
English Last Emperor covers Chen 後主 (AD 582–589), Later Tang 末帝 (AD 934–936), and Later Liang 末帝 (AD 913–923); title reuse across dynasties, not one person.
Both Liao 合術 / Heshu in the 1060s–1070s (Yelü official AD 1063–1066 vs tribal leader AD 1073), but dossier lacks shared offices, kin, or other links beyond the short name.
